batchName: Empire: Tiberius and Caligula (AD 14-41) - Easy Batch 1

questions.question: In 6 BC, on the verge of becoming Rome's second most powerful man, where did Tiberius abruptly retire?
questions.explanation: Tiberius withdrew to Rhodes, a Greek island off the coast of modern Turkey. Historians still debate why he walked away at that moment.
questions.sourceQuote: In 6 BC, on the verge of becoming the second most powerful man in Rome, he abruptly retired to Rhodes, a Greek island off the coast of modern Turkey.

questions.question: What unprecedented honour did Caligula give his beloved sister after her death in AD 38?
options: He named a province after her
He put her face on every coin
He buried her in Augustus's mausoleum
questions.explanation: Caligula declared his sister a goddess. She was the first Roman woman to receive that honour.
questions.sourceQuote: That year his beloved sister died, and he made her a goddess, the first Roman woman so honoured.

questions.question: Who wrote nearly all the surviving accounts of Tiberius and Caligula?
options: Senators and officials writing long afterwards
Palace servants writing at the time
Christian monks of the Middle Ages
questions.explanation: Most of our information comes from senators and officials writing long after the events, men with little love for emperors. That bias shapes the image of both rulers.
questions.sourceQuote: Nearly everything we know about Tiberius and Caligula comes from senators and officials writing long afterwards, men with little love for emperors.

questions.question: Ancient writers agree on when and where Tiberius died. What do they disagree about?
questions.explanation: He died on 16 March AD 37 at Misenum, but accounts of how vary. Some say he was smothered, some blame Caligula, and some contemporaries describe a natural death.
questions.sourceQuote: Ancient writers agree on when and where, but not how.

questions.question: How did Tiberius mainly protect the empire's borders as emperor?
questions.explanation: Tiberius avoided expensive conquests and strengthened the frontiers with bases and diplomacy instead. Whatever senators thought of him, he was an efficient administrator.
questions.sourceQuote: He avoided costly conquests, strengthening the frontiers with new bases and diplomacy instead.

questions.question: When Augustus died in AD 14, what did the mutinous Rhine legions try to do?
options: March on Rome to restore the Republic
questions.explanation: The Rhine legions, angry over unpaid bonuses, tried to make their commander Germanicus emperor. He refused.
questions.sourceQuote: When Augustus died in AD 14, those legions mutinied over unpaid bonuses and tried to proclaim Germanicus emperor.

questions.question: Who murdered Caligula in AD 41?
options: Agents of the governor of Syria
Officers of his own Praetorian Guard
questions.explanation: Caligula was stabbed by officers of his own Praetorian Guard. His German bodyguards arrived too late and killed several bystanders in their fury.
questions.sourceQuote: The killers were officers of his own Praetorian Guard.

questions.question: According to tradition, where was Caligula's uncle found before the Praetorians proclaimed him emperor?
options: Praying in the Temple of Jupiter
questions.explanation: Tradition says a guardsman found Caligula's uncle hiding behind a curtain in the palace. The Praetorians made him emperor and the Senate gave way.
questions.sourceQuote: According to tradition, a guardsman found Caligula's uncle hiding behind a palace curtain; the Praetorians proclaimed him emperor and the Senate gave way.

questions.question: Why did Roman crowds chant "To the Tiber with Tiberius!" after his death?
options: He had drowned in the Tiber
Criminals' bodies were thrown into the river
His villa stood on the Tiber's banks
He had ordered the river dredged
questions.explanation: The crowds wanted his body treated like a criminal's and dumped in the river. The Senate also refused him the divine honours Augustus had received.
questions.sourceQuote: The Senate refused him the divine honours given to Augustus, and crowds chanted "To the Tiber with Tiberius!", because criminals' bodies were thrown into the river.

questions.question: Where did Caligula order a statue of himself to be set up, a blasphemy for Jews?
questions.explanation: Caligula ordered his statue placed in the Temple in Jerusalem. He also enjoyed dressing up as gods, including Jupiter.
questions.sourceQuote: More dangerously, he ordered his statue set up in the Temple in Jerusalem, a blasphemy for Jews.
